title: Smt. Shanti Devi v. Managing Director, Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran & Anr.
coram: V.K. Shukla, A.C.J. & Mahesh Chandra Tripathi, J.
headnote: A consumer who has admittedly consumed electricity cannot be permitted to continue using it without clearing the bills; where payment has not been made, disconnection is inevitable, and the plea that no bill was ever raised does not entitle the consumer to free consumption. The writ court declined to interfere, leaving the consumer to have her dispute resolved under the Electricity Act, 2003 and the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

holding_units.topic: No free consumption; disconnection for non-payment inevitable, dispute to be resolved under the Code
holding_units.question: Can a consumer who consumed electricity resist disconnection on the plea that no bill was raised?
holding_units.holding: No. A consumer who has consumed electricity cannot use it without clearing the bills; on non-payment disconnection is inevitable, and the plea that no bill was raised gives no right to free consumption. The Court did not interfere, relegating the consumer to the billing-dispute remedy under the Act and the Code.
holding_units.limiting_facts: Connection disconnected; consumer admitted consuming electricity but said no bill had been raised.

principle_tags.application: A consumer who consumed electricity must clear the bills; non-payment justifies disconnection, and the absence of a raised bill is no licence for free consumption - the remedy is to resolve the billing dispute under the Code.
